scope.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: n and m are integers with n≥1 and m≥1.

binders.type: real scalar, existentially quantified separately at each (x,t)

binders.type: compact subset of R^n, existentially quantified

hypotheses.statement:
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

source.statement: For every t>0, the density e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. In particular E(t)=E(s) for all s,t>0. The density is |u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|^2 with Euclidean norms, and E(t) is its spatial Lebesgue integral, with no factor 1/2. No assertion at time zero is made.

correspondence.explanation: Positive integers n,m are exactly the naturals with H001; Space n and Space m are the usual real Euclidean spaces with n and m coordinates and L2 norms, and Fin n is a reindexing of 1,...,n. Restriction of total u to t>0 gives the source map; conversely any source map can be extended arbitrarily to nonpositive times. ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ on the open positive space-time set is exactly joint C∞ there and imposes no analytic or nonpositive-time condition. Locality makes all defined time/coordinate derivatives independent of that extension. H003/H004 preserve both unit norms; H005 is pointwise existential real scalar normality, with no regularity imposed on a; H006 retains a single compact C for each whole closed positive interval, allowed to depend on its endpoints, and one globally fixed q. Under integrability, Mathlib's real Bochner integral is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral, using standard Euclidean volume; density is exactly |u_t|² plus the finite sum |∂j u|², with no factor 1/2. The first conjunct states integrability, actual differentiability and derivative zero at every positive time; the second is the complete two-time conservation claim. These assertions restrict to the source target, and the source assertions imply the Lean ones for any total extension since every positive time has an open neighborhood within the domain. No assertion at time zero is added.
